authoritativeAccess.name: Rockhouse public access
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: AGFC and The Nature Conservancy establish the named site's public identity and ownership. Natural Atlas independently maps Rockhouse Boat Launch at 36.28193372205891, -93.6639968409015 and classifies it as a gravel launch on Rockhouse Creek and the Kings River. At that exact point, current Esri World Imagery visibly shows the gravel access road and turnaround terminating at the west bank; a candidate-specific National Map query places it about 107 feet from the Kings River NHD centerline. The older local route-guide coordinate is rejected because it lands about 0.8 mile south in forest. This evidence class is retained for expert-reviewed corrections but is not whitelisted for unattended auto-apply.
authoritativeAccess.coordinateText: Water edge where the mapped Rockhouse gravel launch road meets the west bank of the Kings River

authoritativeFacilityAnchor.name: Rockhouse public access
authoritativeFacilityAnchor.extractionMethod: AGFC states that its McIlroy Madison County WMA property joins the Kings River at Rockhouse Access, and The Nature Conservancy independently identifies Rockhouse as the AGFC-owned public access just upstream from the preserve. Kings River Arkansas describes a gravel road, ample parking, and a large gravel-bar launch near Rockhouse Creek. The facility anchor is the center of the unmistakable gravel turnaround connected to the independently mapped Rockhouse Boat Launch in current Esri World Imagery; it is stored separately from the shoreline water entry. This evidence class records official access identity plus transparent aerial derivation and is intentionally excluded from the unattended auto-apply source whitelist.
authoritativeFacilityAnchor.coordinateText: Center of the gravel vehicle turnaround immediately west of the Rockhouse shoreline landing in current Esri World Imagery

The current North Dakota Game and Fish Department inventory identifies the matching active Grand Forks Park District poured-concrete ramp as ObjectID 1427 at 47.90888410499237, -97.02268528004571. Current Esri World Imagery shows that official point on the upper ramp; the coordinate below is the adjacent water-side end of the same visible concrete ramp, about 79 feet away. The distinct official facility anchor is preserved by provider ndgf_lincoln_drive_park_ramp_access_anchor.

authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: The City of Columbus lease exhibit outlines the public access corridor from Southeast 9th Street to a unique sand-bank entry beside a wooded parcel. The exhibit is south-up; its rail line, canal, access road, wooded parcel, and braided-bank geometry were aligned to current satellite imagery before selecting the water-side end of the mapped corridor. Nebraska Game and Parks independently identifies this terminal access as lying on the Platte River about one mile downstream from the mouth of the Loup. Fresh candidate-centered NHD queries must verify the Platte River flowline, water polygon, and zero-gap Loup-Platte confluence topology before this map-derived point can be applied.

authoritativeAccess.officialName: Platte River State Park Decker Creek canoe/kayak access

Decker Creek canoe and kayak access
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: Nebraska Game and Parks identifies the canoe/kayak stop a few yards from the mouth of Decker Creek and publishes a photograph of the graded landing. Its Platte River Water Trail article gives the route topology: paddlers turn from the Platte up Decker Creek, pass under the railroad bridge, and reach the stop; the site was built as a river-accessible stop rather than a normal vehicle put-in/take-out, though boats may be wheeled down a maintenance road. The official photograph matches the uniquely shaped gravel landing, riprap, curved paved path, and footbridge visible in current Esri World Imagery. The coordinate is the water edge of that landing on the west bank of Decker Creek, immediately south of the footbridge.

Plum Creek Landing
authoritativeAccess.extractionMethod: The Wisconsin DNR public-access inventory identifies feature 835 as Plum Creek Landing, a state-owned carry-in on the Kickapoo River, and Crawford County independently lists the Plum Creek/Kickapoo Wild Woods Canoe Landing. Wisconsin River Trips documents the exact Plum Creek-to-Highway-60 trip, while Miles Paddled's Plum-Creek-to-Wauzeka report publishes 43.11429, -90.91274 for this put-in and 43.08471, -90.87906 for the distinct Wauzeka take-out. Current Esri World Imagery places the DNR coordinate at the water-side edge of the visible gravel turnaround. Candidate-centered NHD evidence independently places it inside the river polygon and 18 feet from the Kickapoo flowline, so the exact DNR coordinate is retained as the water entry.
